scenario: A person types for about six hours a day and is trying to understand why mechanical keyboards range from about 40 dollars to premium prices, even when listings use similar broad switch labels. They want to know where the extra spend goes, which differences can affect sustained typing and ownership, which mainly affect sound or hobby experience, and how to set a sensible purchase boundary. The available material includes catalog examples from 39.99 to 149.99 dollars, community experience about switches, sound, modification effort, quality control, and street prices, plus background on layout, posture, construction, and durability.
target: Explain what the observed price spread actually buys, why a switch label cannot stand in for a whole keyboard, and how layout, posture, construction, quietness, tactile feel, modification effort, and ownership risks should be compared for six-hour daily use. End with a least-expensive-passing-option rule and say clearly why the available material cannot name one universal price cutoff or objectively best board.
